passages.text: Financial Condition and Results of Operations The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations focuses on and is intended to clarify the results of our operations, certain changes in our financial position, liquidity, capital structure and business developments during the fiscal years ended December 27, 2025 and December 28, 2024 and a year-to-year comparison of these two fiscal years. This discussion should be read in conjunction with, and is qualified by reference to, the other related information including, but not limited to, the audited consolidated financial statements (including the notes thereto), the description of our business, all as set forth in this Form 10-K, as well as the risk factors discussed above in Item 1A. Discussion regarding our results of operations for the fiscal year ended December 30, 2023 and a year-to-year comparison between the fiscal years ended December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023 can be found in Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 28, 2024. As previously noted, the discussion set forth below, as well as other portions of this Form 10-K, contain statements concerning potential future events. Readers can identify these forward-looking statements by their use of such verbs as “expects,” “anticipates,” “believes”, or similar verbs or conjugations of such verbs. If any of our assumptions on which the statements are based prove incorrect or should unanticipated circumstances arise, our actual results could materially differ from those anticipated by such forward-looking statements. The differences could be caused by a number of factors or combination of factors including, but not limited to, those discussed above in Item 1A. Readers are strongly encouraged to consider those factors when evaluating any such forward-looking statement. Except as may be required by law, we do not undertake to update any forward-looking statements in this Form 10-K. Garmin’s fiscal year is based on a 52- or 53-week period ending on the last Saturday of the calendar year. Fiscal years 2025, 2024, and 2023 each contained 52 weeks. Unless otherwise stated, all years and dates refer to the Company’s fiscal year and fiscal periods. Unless the context otherwise requires, references in this document to “we”, “us”, “our”, “the Company” and similar terms refer to Garmin Ltd. and its subsidiaries. Unless otherwise indicated, dollar amounts set forth in the tables are in thousands, except per share data. Overview The Company is a leading worldwide producer of innovative products, many of which feature Global Positioning System (GPS) navigation, services and applications that are designed for people who live an active lifestyle. Garmin is organized in the five operating segments of fitness, outdoor, aviation, marine, and auto OEM, which represent the primary markets served by the Company. These operating segments also represent our reportable segments. The Company’s Chief Executive Officer, who has been identified as the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM), allocates resources and assesses performance of each operating segment individually. credit_strengths.text: Garmin's operating margin sits well above the Information Technology sector median, reflecting pricing power across its fitness, outdoor, aviation, marine and auto OEM segments. Revenue and operating income have expanded steadily over the three-year trend, evidencing durable demand for GPS-enabled devices and services rather than a single-year spike.

Liquidity is a core strength: the current ratio exceeds the sector median, with current assets covering current liabilities multiple times over. Cash balances and internally generated funds provide ample cushion, and the absence of tagged borrowings suggests the capital structure is essentially unlevered, leaving capacity for investment or shareholder returns.

key_risks.text: The risk-factor passage flags forward-looking exposure to assumptions about demand, supply and market conditions that could cause actual results to differ materially. For a hardware-led GPS franchise with five reporting segments, such variability could pressure revenue and margins if consumer or aviation demand softens, weakening the cash generation that underpins credit quality.

No borrowing tags were reported for the balance-sheet date, so debt, net debt, leverage and interest coverage cannot be computed from the bundle. This is a material data gap: without confirmed funded debt or interest expense, we cannot verify the capital structure or assess refinancing and maturity risk, and the indicative financial risk profile remains unrated.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating cash flow comfortably exceeds capital expenditure, producing strong free cash flow that covers the disclosed dividend outlay. This internally funded model means debt service, if any exists, is supported by recurring cash generation rather than external refinancing, and the cash conversion profile compares favorably with sector peers.

Because interest expense and debt are not tagged, interest coverage and free-cash-flow-to-debt ratios are unavailable, so we cannot quantify headroom against sector median coverage. Judgementally, the EBITDA proxy and cash position suggest substantial capacity to absorb modest borrowings, but confirmation of any lease-adjusted or off-balance-sheet obligations is required before relying on this view.

overall_credit_view.text: Garmin presents a high-quality, cash-generative credit profile: revenue and operating income are growing, margins exceed the sector median, and the balance sheet carries substantial cash with a current ratio above peers. The absence of reported borrowings implies minimal leverage, though this remains unconfirmed and the indicative risk profile is not a rating.

Forward-looking, we expect free cash flow to continue funding dividends and internal investment, with leverage staying low absent a debt-funded acquisition. The key analytical gap is the missing debt and interest expense disclosure; until confirmed, we treat refinancing risk as low but unverified, and would revisit the view if borrowings or shareholder distributions materially increase.

credit_strengths.text: Garmin 的營業利潤率遠高於資訊科技行業中位數，反映其在健身、戶外、航空、航海及汽車 OEM 各分部均具定價能力。收入及營業利潤在三年趨勢中穩步擴張，證明市場對 GPS 設備及服務的需求持久，而非單一年度的短暫急升。
流動性是核心優勢：流動比率高於行業中位數，流動資產以數倍覆蓋流動負債。現金結餘及內部產生資金提供充足緩衝，而並無標記借款，顯示資本結構基本上並無槓桿，為投資或股東回報留有空間。

key_risks.text: 風險因素章節指出前瞻性風險，涉及對需求、供應及市況的假設，可能導致實際結果與預期出現重大差異。對於擁有五個報告分部的硬件主導 GPS 業務，若消費者或航空需求轉弱，此等波動可能對收入及利潤率構成壓力，削弱支撐信貸質素的現金產生能力。
於資產負債表日期並無呈報借款標記，因此無法從資料組合計算債務、淨債務、槓桿及利息覆蓋率。此為重大數據缺口：在未確認有息債務或利息開支的情況下，我們無法核實資本結構或評估再融資及到期風險，而指示性財務風險狀況仍屬未評級。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 經營現金流穩步超過資本開支，產生強勁自由現金流，足以覆蓋已披露的股息支出。此內部融資模式意味著債務償付（如存在）由經常性現金產生支撐，而非依賴外部再融資，且現金轉換狀況與行業同業相比具優勢。
由於利息開支及債務並無標記，利息覆蓋率及自由現金流對債務比率無法取得，因此我們無法量化相對行業中位數覆蓋率的緩衝空間。按判斷，EBITDA 代理指標及現金狀況顯示有相當能力吸納適度借款，但在依賴此觀點前，須確認任何租賃調整或表外責任。

overall_credit_view.text: Garmin 呈現高質量、現金產生能力強的信用狀況：收入及營業利潤正在增長，利潤率超過行業中位數，且資產負債表持有大量現金，流動比率高於同業。並無呈報借款意味槓桿極低，惟此仍未確認，且指示性風險狀況並非評級。
前瞻而言，我們預期自由現金流將繼續為股息及內部投資提供資金，在沒有債務融資收購的情況下槓桿維持低位。關鍵分析缺口為缺失的債務及利息開支披露；在確認之前，我們將再融資風險視為低但未經核實，並會在借款或股東分派大幅增加時重新審視此觀點。
